result.title: Event-based Action Recognition by Pre-Training on Multi-Frame Representations
result.summary: Action recognition is a crucial task in domains like robotics, patient monitoring, or surveillance. Recently, event-based action recognition has attracted much attention due to the event camera's ability to capture fast motions and its improved privacy over conventional vision cameras. While frame-based event representations work well for short event sequences, their discriminative ability declines sharply with longer and more complex event sequences. In this work, we introduce a multi-frame representation that greatly improves recognition performance over its single-frame counterpart. We adopt a masked auto-encoding framework to pre-train a Vision Transformer using a sparsity-aware masking algorithm and token selection mechanism to improve downstream performance and control computational complexity. We also introduce multiple mask tokens for the decoder with a position-aware attention mechanism, leading to further improved performance. Our proposed method shows impressive performance for challenging long-duration and complex event sequences, yielding state-of-the-art performance on THU-EACT-50 CHL and DailyDVS-200.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究基于事件相机的动作识别，提出多帧事件表示替代单帧表示，并以稀疏感知掩码和 token 选择机制预训练 Vision Transformer，还引入多 mask token 与位置感知注意力，在长时复杂事件序列上取得领先结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其稀疏掩码与 token 选择属于按信息量裁剪视觉输入、控制计算量的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与动态计算预算分配的设计。
